chapter: California, Cats and the Fiddle, the Tatum trio
title: New York jam sessions; Charlie Christian plays his four-string guitar
summary: At Clark Monroe's and Morton's he was learning among great players, and Charlie Christian once took his guitar and played it.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: ... I was just learning how to play -- I used to go down to Clark-Monroe's, told, Wilson used to be there. All the great guys used to come there. I had in my mind to play ... they asked me --- whisper it in my ear, say "hey man, look I'm gonna play somethin' here so you lay out, hear?" That musta been how bad I was. But I was determined. I couldn't keep up with some of them cats. But I finally found myself doin' enough to keep up with them, and get a little gig every week end hopefully 5 dollars, 3 dollars, and There were some good times. I wasn't no dog-eat-dog like it is now. You could walk over to central park and sit out there and sleep out there all night, and nobody would bother you. Walk the streets at night.
Did you ever play with Charlie Christian

Didn't I tell you he played my guitar? -- At Morton's, everybody used to meet at Morton's -- Monk, Joe Guy, Kenny Clarke, his brother -- a lot of people don't know his brother played bass. Charlie Christian was there all the time. I'm just learnin' how to play. So I come in and Charlie has taken my guitar

And played it, played the hell out of it, 4 strings -- he played it. And that made me wanna play that much worse, ha, ha. He was a nice cat. He was tickled at me for the 4 strings. He said, "man why don't you get yourself six strings". I say, "I can hardly play these four, no sense of six." He played it all right, old Gibson I had. But he could play, I got some tapes around here. Dan Morgenstern has got the tapes. He's got the records --
